decision.title: XPath Full Text: a grammar of the feature; parser part extensions; the package's EXPath prefixes (packet 7.12d)

body.p: , after , , , , , , . Amends ("XPath's Full Text is not implemented"). Verified as asks: the debug preset, the unit, CLI and QT4 driver tests touched, clang-tidy on the files changed, tools/check-call-cycles.py, the wasm preset's JavaScript tests, and the whole QT4 XP40 and XQ40 suites with the release driver, compared case by case.

item.p: The grammar: XQuery and XPath Full Text 3.0, Appendix B (XPath 3.0 with Full Text) applied to XPath 4.0 as grammars/xquery applies Appendix A: FTContainsExpr as the operand of ComparisonExpr, FTScoreVar in the for bindings (SimpleForBinding, after XPath 4.0's positional variable), Pragma for FTExtensionSelection. XPath's let bindings take no score variable (B [13]: XPST0003). The productions are written once, in grammars/xpath/full_text.js; grammars/xquery uses them (its generated parser is byte-identical) and so does the new grammars/xpath_full_text.

Why a grammar of its own: the productions in grammars/xpath grow its compiled parser from 310,662 to 505,223 bytes of wasm32 code and data (-Os, +194,561), all of it in the core sxml.wasm, against 's "keep the core lean". As a parser of its own, named only by the feature full-text (sxml_full_text_operations.xpath_parser_part), it costs the core nothing and the full module and the CLI 500,913 bytes (the full XPath parser again, with Full Text's states). Rejected: the XQuery parser for XPath text (string literal references, direct constructors, the namespace axis and the reserved names differ).

's place for XPath is the grammar: without the feature, sxml_xpath_compile parses with grammars/xpath, which has no Full Text syntax, so the text is XPST0003 there, as for a processor without Full Text. With the feature it parses with the feature's part, then runs the feature's static rules (check_rules: XQST0089, FTST0009, FTST0019, XQST0079), then lowers. XSLT's own expressions keep grammars/xpath (Full Text extends XPath and XQuery, not XSLT); xsl:evaluate, which compiles through sxml_xpath_compile, has it.

Parser part extensions (glossary ; src/xpath_ast_internal.h): a parser part may name an extension, a part whose node types and fields the walker looks up after the part's and whose apply_token it offers a token after the part's. Full Text's node types, fields and tokens move from src/xquery_parse.c to src/full_text_parse.c (sxml_full_text_parser_part), the extension of XQuery's part and of the feature's XPath part, whose own tables are empty: one definition for both grammars. XQuery's apply_token leaves Full Text's nodes to the extension.

Lowering: the lowering part full_text serves XPath too (its contains rule; the rule's step is the feature's, as for XQuery). The core's for binding (src/xpath_lower.c) binds a score variable after the feature's for score procedure (XQuery's, through the new operation call_for_score, so the core does not link it), before the binding's variables are in scope, as XQuery's for clause does.

The QT4 driver supports fullText, fullText-ignore, fullText-units and fullText-defaults for XPath too. The ft-* cases are all XQ10+, so none runs under XP40. Measured by running them through the XPath API (the spec rule bypassed in a private build, not committed): the 48 written as XPath expressions all pass; the other 637 use XQuery syntax (626 declare variables, 10 use constructors, 1 order by) and are XPST0003 there, as they should be.

Numbers: release, whole runs, 7749770 against the change: XP40 32,655 passed, 34 wrong errors, 82 failed; XQ40 45,914, 55, 239; no case changed. tools/qt4-parse-check.py --spec XP40 classifies the 32,928 applicable cases alike with grammars/xpath and grammars/xpath_full_text (0 false rejects, 2 false accepts).

Sizes (wasm preset, stripped / gzipped, before and after d25980e): sxml.wasm 2,087,567 / 729,646 to 2,088,782 / 730,104 (+1,215: the score binding 668, the extension loops 166, the contains rule 193), no budget raised; sxml-full.wasm 7,116,988 / 1,640,375 to 7,619,484 / 1,684,247; the CLI 8,711,495 / 1,921,864 to 9,213,991 / 1,965,878. Budgets (): the full module 8,000,000 / 2,800,000 (was 7,500,000 / 2,625,000), the CLI 9,500,000 / 2,100,000 (was 9,000,000 / 2,000,000). The core's size baseline is refreshed at 6c994b2 (it also takes in about 10 KB that other packets added since : xml_input, ir_global_read, the XML grammar).

The JavaScript package's EXPath prefixes: as the sxml command binds bin and file (EXPath Binary 4.0, 1.5; EXPath File 4.0, 1.7), the package binds, for XPath and XQuery, the prefix of each feature the processor has: bin with expath-binary, file with expath-file (which the package's modules do not link). The caller's namespaces may rebind them. In TypeScript (src/index.ts), from the processor's feature list, so the core module, which has no feature, links nothing more.
Left: the declaration of sxml_full_text_feature() in include/sxml/xquery.h still says "for XQuery" (see Proposed); the scanner is instantiated once per grammar (5,577 bytes again in the full module).
